ipa.curves._cross_currency_curves.triangulate_definitions.search.Definition

API endpoint for Financial Contract analytics, that returns calculations relevant to each contract type.

Available as lseg.data.content.ipa.curves._cross_currency_curves.triangulate_definitions.search.Definition.

Syntax

Definition(
    *,
    base_currency: OptStr = None,
    base_index_name: OptStr = None,
    curve_tag: OptStr = None,
    quoted_currency: OptStr = None,
    quoted_index_name: OptStr = None,
    valuation_date: OptStr = None,
    extended_params: ExtendedParams = None,
) -> None

Parameters

Parameter Type Required Default Description
base_currency OptStr No None The base currency pair. It is expressed in ISO 4217 alphabetical format (e.g., 'EUR').
base_index_name OptStr No None The name of the floating rate index (e.g., 'ESTR') applied to the base currency.
curve_tag OptStr No None A user-defined string to identify the interest rate curve. it can be used to link output results to the curve definition. limited to 40 characters. only alphabetic, numeric and '- _.#=@' characters are supported.
quoted_currency OptStr No None The quoted currency pair. It is expressed in ISO 4217 alphabetical format (e.g., 'USD').
quoted_index_name OptStr No None The name of the floating rate index (e.g., 'SOFR') applied to the quoted currency.
valuation_date OptStr No None The valuation date.
extended_params ExtendedParams No None If necessary other parameters.

Methods

get_data

Sends a request to the Data Platform to retrieve the predefined data.

get_data(session: Session | None = None) -> T

Parameters

Sends an asynchronous request to the Data Platform to retrieve the predefined data.

async get_data_async(
    session: Session | None = None,

Parameters

Parameter Type Required Default Description

Example

from lseg.data.content.ipa.curves._cross_currency_curves import triangulate_definitions
definition = triangulate_definitions.search.Definition(
    base_currency="EUR",
    quoted_currency="CHF"
)
response = definition.get_data()

# Using get_data_async

import asyncio
task = definition.get_data_async()
response = asyncio.run(task)
